audio_caption: A woman speaks passionately, her voice rising and falling as she discusses being overlooked in history despite her capabilities. She mentions "Kellyanne," and "Donald Trump" in relation to a presidential campaign. Her tone is assertive and somewhat aggrieved, but also proud. She describes how "men in this complex, in this White House," tried to stop her. She mentions surviving over everyone. The sound of music begins playing in the background, possibly meant to emphasize the emotions of the speaker.

The audio clip begins with a female speaker reflecting on her time working for President Obama. She discusses how changes, like the Obamacare website's malfunction or conflicts with Congress, affected his approval ratings and support within the Democratic party.  In contrast, she notes that President Trump's supporters seem "bought in" and deeply connected to what they gain from his presidency. Another female voice enters, asserting that "most people in this country see themselves as an outsider to the system," and that Donald Trump retains this quality. She argues that the Democratic party's nomination of Joe Biden signals a lack of "forward-looking, visionary, new generation change."

The audio clip starts with a female speaker discussing former president Trump as the "incumbent outsider" in a conversational tone. Another female voice joins in, suggesting that Joe Biden would be "the hardest one" to label as "part of the radical left" due to his long history, emphasizing that his story doesn't fit the radical left narrative. She describes him as "a brief and loss and a man who's done right by his family," expressing respect. The first female speaker chimes in, saying "It's a pretty good part of his story" before the second speaker resumes, expressing that there is "no reason that he should be doing the Bernie manifesto and listening to AOC on Green New Deal." Another female speaker then mentions "16, you know, what happened, what happened happened." Then she mentions that "18, a lot of women left the republicans, voted for democrats in the midterm."

The clip opens with the sound of speech, consisting of a female speaker questioning Biden's support and emphasizing, "did they?" In response, another female speaker, in a slightly more energetic tone, points out Biden is "still doing better," highlighting the "gender gap" and advertising attempts to "frighten women into supporting Trump". The audio transitions to an unclear end.

The audio clip begins with a female speaker discussing the "gender gap" and opining against "women's issues," citing her own experience. Another female speaker expresses agreement. The first woman then accuses men of not thinking women capable of certain things. The second woman states "you're not" and then again agrees with the first speaker that there's "no such thing as a women's issue." Then, the second woman notes that Biden is performing well with women.

The audio clip features a woman speaking about a president keeping promises, stating that "women look at the progress report," and that "ladies know we love men who keep their promises". The speaker expresses that it's important for men to keep their word, noting that the president has done more in 47 months than another person did in 47 years. The tone is affirmative and supportive. A second woman, named Jennifer, is addressed during the speech.

The clip starts with a female speaker asking about "the easiest way to contrast." Another female replies, "you personally, really believe in Donald Trump, right?" And continues to say that she believes in America. The woman lists several things that democrats may see, such as the US leading in world deaths due to COVID, the greatest economic downturn since the great depression, and "cynically, the democrats believe they can win an election." The speaker continues by saying, "Isn't it so sad that they see political opportunism in a pandemic? We don't." She believes they see a dual medical and financial crisis. A male speaker interjects, saying "I think Biden probably sees a vacuum of leadership that he could step into." The first female speaker responds that it all turned around 5 or 6 weeks ago, when "President Trump said to the country and tweeted out, I'm wearing a mask, I want you to wear a mask." She mentions Trump's tweet again at the end of the clip.

The clip opens with a female speaker recounting a conversation where she predicted a tweet would gain 200,000 likes, attributing this to the public's interest in political tweets and directional advice. She mentions the resumption of coronavirus briefings, urging them to be concise and technical. She further describes the president's decision to cancel the live convention and rallies, characterizing it as leadership. Her tone is conversational and persuasive. Transitioning, she notes the Democrats' plans to attend Nantucket, Martha's Vineyard, and the Hamptons before exclaiming, "Holy crap, this guy is coming back!" She then shifts to discussing the racial unrest coinciding with the convention. The clip contains background sounds of speech, adding to the conversational atmosphere.

The audio begins with a woman's voice, speaking in a serious tone, referencing a video of George Floyd, then asking about a video of Jacob Blake. A second woman responds in a similar tone, noting an investigation and the rioting and looting in cities like Minneapolis, Portland and Seattle, where people have lost their lives overnight and are armed with huge firearms, and whether they welcome the unrest in their campaign. This exchange is underscored by a somber, melancholic string section. The mood remains serious and contemplative.

The audio clip begins with a female voice expressing concern about the country being divided and cities being destroyed by non-peaceful protesters. She then directly asks whether peaceful protesters killed people overnight in Kenosha with firearms. In response, another female voice states that they did not before the first voice clarifies their stance, questioning if the actions were murder. The clip ends with a somber musical tone playing in the background. The music sounds melancholic. There is also a sound that sounds like a train whistle and an unidentifiable whooshing noise.

The audio begins with a conversation. One woman speaks, expressing hope that "President Trump" did not "try to win by capturing a medal," or "bringing people to a side." Another woman replies, calling it "not true." The first speaker continues, adding that "people voted for him who had never voted Democrat." The second speaker responds that "the vast majority of his support is white working Americans." She then questions why the first woman is "denouncing them" and states that they "matter." The first woman expresses that she has "respect for the white working class." Then, the second woman mentions there's often "the raised eyebrow, the furled lip," specifically regarding "Trump's supporters." Background chatter can be heard throughout the conversation.

The clip begins with a woman speaking with noticeable emotion in her voice. She describes feeling triggered "a fire in my belly and bile on my throat" when people from her upbringing are mocked or ridiculed. She mentions specific examples like going to church or owning a firearm. In the background are sounds suggestive of a quiet indoor setting.

The audio begins with a female speaker mentioning the term "hidden undercover Trump voter" and that there are "more of them", stating that they will surprise people in the ballot box. She suggests that the president will be way ahead after the conventions. The speaking tone is conversational. Following this dialogue, the music starts with a tense, suspenseful atmosphere, featuring prominent synth sounds, building up anticipation. Towards the end a distorted electronic sound effect plays.
